// expected.txt - what the host answered for -[<class> init] on every class the registry carries a
// row for. Generated by tests/backports/host/intents-init/run.sh with the golden argument left
// off; re-read that comment before changing a line here, because a line changes when the HOST
// changes and not when the port does.
//
// One line per class: name, then own-or-inherit, then object/nil/threw, then the property reads,
// then how many of those read non-nil, then which. `own` means the class declares -init itself,
// `inherit` means it takes NSObject's; the port's generated body always forwards to the
// superclass's IMP, so an `own` line is a row whose body is not the answer the host gives.
//
// Read these three groups before believing the rest:
//
//   -init own 64, inherited 53.  The 64 are the rows whose `implemented` rests on a body that
//   differs from the host's, and that difference was invisible until this harness ran.
//
//   INRelevanceProvider raises, with the reason "INRelevanceProvider cannot be initialized
//   directly with -init, initialize a subclass instead."  The header marks the class's -init
//   NS_UNAVAILABLE and the framework refuses it in the same breath. The port answers with an
//   object instead, which is the row's `effect` and is a deliberate difference, not an oversight.
//
//   INCancelRideIntentResponse and INSendRideFeedbackIntentResponse answer nil, with the system's
//   own "Unable to initialize '<name>'. Please make sure that your intent definition file is
//   valid."  Both are intent RESPONSES whose class the framework wants an .intent definition for.
//
//   Five classes answer an object with a property that is NOT nil: INListRideOptionsIntentResponse
//   .rideOptions, INObjectCollection.allItems, INPerson.displayName,
//   INSearchForMessagesIntentResponse.messages and INSendMessageIntentResponse.sentMessages. The
//   registry's rows say every property is nil; on these five it is not, and the property named is
//   the answer each one computes rather than stores.
//
// macOS 27.0 build 26A428, arm64, Foundation + Intents, measured with sw_vers on the run that
// wrote these lines. run.sh prints the host it measured on beside the verdict, so a reader can tell a
// stale golden from a host that changed without being told which one it is. A different host answers
// with its own numbers and the guard above fails until this file is rewritten.
